item.title: Advances in Agentic Computer Graphics
item.description: Computer graphics is built on code. Large language model (LLM) agents can now generate graphics code and iteratively refine it through various feedback. This capability opens the door to a potentially new paradigm of computer graphics, with graphics algorithms increasingly built around agentic systems to automate progressively complex tasks. Over the past years, research on agentic graphics has expanded rapidly across a diverse range of tasks. This rapid growth makes it increasingly difficult for manual literature reviews to keep pace with new developments. item.title: GraCo: A Unified Toolkit of Graph Coarsening Algorithms and Metrics
item.description: Graph coarsening aims to reduce a graph to a smaller one that preserves chosen properties of the original. It is increasingly used to scale graph learning to large graphs, as a non-differentiable step applied once before training. Many coarsening methods have been proposed in recent years, each with its own implementation, notation and evaluation. In this work, we introduce GraCo, a unified toolkit of graph coarsening methods. It relies on a single definition: a coarsening is fixed by a partition of the nodes and by the Laplacian the coarsened graph is consistent with.
